title: Privacy, tenant rights and multidisciplinary handoff
audience: Coordinators, support workers and trained cleaners who may be asked to work in a home affected by hoarding or environmental neglect, as part of an authorised support plan. Not a qualification or authority to clear a property, dispose of a resident's belongings, enter by force, or provide welfare or clinical support.
learningOutcomes: Refuse a request for information that has no authorised purpose, and record the refusal.
Write a handoff record that separates agreed, done, unresolved and referred items.
Send information only to authorised recipients through the agreed channel.

instruction.heading: Scope of this lesson
instruction.body: This lesson covers the limits of information handling and referral. It does not give legal advice on tenancy, guardianship, privacy or safeguarding. Completing it does not qualify a worker to make welfare, clinical or safeguarding decisions.

instruction.heading: Only the minimum needed
instruction.body: Collect, keep and share only the information needed for the agreed work, and only where the resident or the lawful authority allows it. The rules on tenancy, safeguarding referral and information sharing differ by jurisdiction, and the coordinator confirms the legal basis for any disclosure. An agency that asks for photographs of every room and copies of personal documents is asking for far more than the work requires. Refuse requests that are not tied to an authorised purpose, and record the refusal and the reason.

instruction.heading: The handoff record
instruction.body: A handoff record states what was agreed, what was done, what is unresolved, who is responsible for each open issue, and what has been referred. Refer welfare, health and safeguarding concerns to the people responsible for them, not to the crew. Give the receiving service only the minimum needed. Mark anything that is unverified as unverified, and never present a person's health, drug use or circumstances as established fact unless a responsible person has confirmed it.

procedure: Confirm the legal basis and the purpose for every item of information requested.
Limit photographs and records to the authorised record.
Refuse requests for personal documents or images that are not tied to an authorised purpose, and record the refusal.
Write the handoff record with agreed scope, done, unresolved, responsible person and referrals.
Send the handoff only to the authorised recipient, through the agreed channel.
Refer welfare, health and safeguarding concerns to the responsible people, and record each referral.

workedExamples.situation: An agency asks for photographs of every room and copies of personal documents.
workedExamples.reasoning: Refuse the requests that are not tied to the agreed work. Check the legal authority, purpose and consent for any private information, and record the decision and the reason.

workedExamples.situation: A service asks for the resident's full medical history for a handoff.
workedExamples.reasoning: Nothing beyond the authorised minimum, and only once the legal basis is confirmed. Refer the health questions to the people responsible for the resident's care, and record the referral.

equipmentAndPpe: Information request log with fields for purpose, legal basis and decision.
Training-only fictional case files. No real personal information is used in this lesson.

commonErrors.error: Sending photographs of the home to people who are not authorised.
commonErrors.prevention: Share only with authorised recipients, and record each disclosure.

commonErrors.error: Recording unverified health or personal details as fact.
commonErrors.prevention: Mark what is unverified, and record the source of every statement.

commonErrors.error: Giving an agency personal documents the work does not need.
commonErrors.prevention: Refuse, and record the refusal with the reason.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Privacy, tenancy and safeguarding obligations depend on the law that applies. This lesson does not set out that law and gives no legal advice.
Completing this lesson does not qualify a worker to make welfare, clinical or safeguarding decisions.

qualityStandard: The learner refuses a request for information that has no authorised purpose.
The learner writes a handoff record with done, unresolved and referred items separated.
The learner sends information only to authorised recipients.
documentationEvidence: Information request log with the purpose, the legal basis and the decision.
Handoff record with agreed, done, unresolved, responsible person and referrals.
Record of each disclosure, with the recipient and the authority.
summary: Collect and share only the minimum needed.
Refuse requests that have no authorised purpose.
Keep the handoff clear about what is unverified.
Refer welfare and health concerns to the responsible people.

knowledgeChecks.question: An agency asks for photographs of every room and copies of personal documents. What is the right response?
options: Send the photographs but keep the documents back.
Refuse the requests that are not tied to the agreed work, and record the refusal and the reason.

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a handoff record separate?
options: Agreed, done, unresolved and referred items.
The crew's hours and the lunch menu.

knowledgeChecks.question: A resident's health information is requested for a handoff. What is correct?
options: Share the full history so the next service is informed.
Share only the authorised minimum, once the legal basis is confirmed, and refer health questions to the responsible people.
Describe the health condition from the crew's own guess.

officialReferences.title: Hoarding and environmental neglect (Department of Families, Fairness and Housing, Victoria, provider page)
officialReferences.covers: Read through a summary tool on 2026-11-03. The page defines hoarding as keeping many things that others think are useless or have little or no value; says hoarding is different from collecting, where collectors are usually well organised and collect one type of thing; and cites the Make Safe guidance for services working with people living with hoarding and environmental neglect. Publisher: Department of Families, Fairness and Housing (Victoria).

moduleAuthority.heading: Module authority and restricted work
moduleAuthority.body: This module is training content. It does not grant authority to enter a home by force, to clear, sort or dispose of a resident's belongings without valid consent, to handle or dispose of hazardous waste, to deal with unstable stacks or structural hazards, or to provide welfare, clinical or safeguarding assessments. Completing this lesson does not give a licence, certificate or approval. Work is done only under an authorised support plan and a written agreement with the resident, within the limits set by the employer and the local law. Tenancy, safeguarding and information-sharing rights are jurisdiction-specific, and fire-risk, structural, pest and hazardous-waste decisions belong to the competent authorities and specialists named in the plan. Where authority or consent is unclear, stop and refer.

stopWorkAndReferral.heading: Stop-work and referral rules for this module
stopWorkAndReferral.body: Stop and refer whenever any of these is true: consent is not specific, documented and current; the resident has objected or withdrawn consent; a party seeks entry by force, nonconsensual disposal or removal of personal documents; a fire-load, ignition, egress or obstruction hazard is present; a stack or structure is unstable; pests, unknown liquids or mouldy goods are present; sharps, chemicals or unknown containers are found; waste would go to general disposal without characterisation; private information is requested without authority; or the work would go beyond the approved plan. Stopping is a valid professional outcome. Record the disagreement, protect the resident's choices and refer the authority dispute before any property is moved.
